lead_raw_text:
The structure of Ca2Si crystallizes in the hexagonal space group P6_3/mmc (No. 194), with a unit cell containing six atoms (Ca4Si2) distributed over two independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Si centers with nine Ca neighbors and Ca centers with ten neighbors (four Ca, six Si), giving a three-dimensional connected network. Validated polyhedron contacts reveal corner- and edge-sharing between Ca 10-vertex polyhedra, and corner-sharing between Ca 10-vertex and Si 9-vertex polyhedra, though these patterns are not exclusive.
